title: Bandit-driven stochastic kernel prober with warmstart fingerprinting
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: We need a low-overhead, online mechanism to pick among multiple kernel implementations (attention kernels, matmul microkernels, fused-attention variants) that adapts to both hardware (GPU arch/FLOPS/SM count) and observed sequence-length distribution. Existing deterministic heuristics are brittle for mixed workloads and do not gracefully explore novel kernel variants.

Goal: Implement a bandit-style stochastic prober that: (1) maintains lightweight fingerprints of machines and workload prefill/decode patterns, (2) warm-starts exploration using offline microbenchmarks and fingerprint similarity, (3) runs background low-cost probes that gather latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs and update a per-model/per-route kernel selection policy, and (4) exposes roll-forward/rollback controls for canarying and safety.

Scope: PoC runtime component + controller + metrics plumbing. Focus on prefill-aware selection (prefill length distribution and KV cache hit rates) and decode-phase policy switching. Do not change model internals. Surface controls via existing kernel advisor config and add a per-route knob for "exploration budget".

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Algorithm: Use a contextual multi-armed bandit (CMAB) with epsilon-greedy warmstart. Context vector includes: GPU family tag, free memory, average prefill seqlen bucket, recent KV-cache hit ratio, and model geometry fingerprint (hidden dims, n_head, rotary/none). This is lightweight and avoids heavy ML infra.
- Warmstart: Use offline microbenchmarks to create a small database of (fingerprint -> prefered kernel ranking). At startup, lookup nearest fingerprints (L2 on normalized numeric fields) to seed the CMAB priors. If no close fingerprint, default to safe low-latency kernel.
- Probing policy: Background probes are rate-limited by per-route exploration_budget and constrained to off-peak tokens. Probes are single-request probes with representative seqlen buckets (8, 64, 256, 1024). Prefer probing on spare capacity to avoid latency regressions.
- Safety: Probes that exceed 2x SLO latency are counted as failed and penalize that arm. We maintain a conservative fallback and allow immediate rollback to previous kernel if 95th percentile latency increases beyond configured delta.
- Storage: Keep only aggregated probe statistics in memory and persist periodic checkpoints to the control-plane KV store for continuity across restarts.

Acceptance criteria:
- PoC finds the empirically best kernel in >70% of microbenchmark cases compared to current static heuristic within 2 hours of deployment for mixed seqlen workloads.
- End-to-end overhead from probing must be <0.5% of total tokens for a busy instance (configurable exploration_budget default 0.2%).
- No customer route sees >3% increase in 95p latency during exploration windows.
- Metrics: per-route kernel_choice_time_series, probe_success_rate, rollback_count, average_latency_delta, and cost_delta.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Microbenchmark harness (ENG): small tool that runs kernels across seqlen buckets and produces canonical fingerprinted profiles. (Deliverable: /confluence/kernel-prober/microbench v1)
2) CMAB runtime component: lightweight module in serving runtime that accepts context and returns kernel choice; integrates with existing kernel selection interface.
3) Controller service: coordinates warmstart lookups, persists aggregated stats, plans probe schedule.
4) Dashboards/Alerts: Grafana panels for probe health, rollback events; alert if rollback_count > 3 in 1h for a route.
5) Canary + Rollout: start on internal dev routes, then opt-in beta customers, then global default when stable.

Open questions:
- Should the context include per-customer QoS tier? (Impacts exploration aggressiveness.)
- How to best represent model geometry fingerprint for mixed-size models (adapter/LoRA)?
- Where to store persisted checkpoints for private deployments (control plane not available)?

Docs + artifacts:
- Proposal: https://confluence.redwood/inference/kernel-prober/proposal-2026
- Microbench results (initial): https://drive.redwood/company/kernel-prober/microbench-2026-02-18.csv
- Design sketch: https://figma.redwood/designs/kernel-prober-flow

Rollout plan and staged releases:
- alpha: runtime-1.20-alpha (internal only) — run on dev cluster, run full microbench and warmstart results.
- beta: runtime-1.20-beta (selected customers) — enable exploration_budget at 0.05% on low-impact routes.
- GA: runtime-1.20 (default exploration_budget 0.2%, opt-out available)

Longer term: Replace epsilon-greedy with a lightweight Thompson-sampling implementation if probe budget allows; add per-tenant policy drift detection and model-specific reward shaping (cost+latency+output-quality).

2026-03-06 - Ava Patel: Design review notes recorded in Confluence. Decided to use numeric normalized fields for fingerprinting instead of hashed strings to allow nearest-neighbour warmstart.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Canary run started on internal-text-route-3. After 24h, CMAB converged to kernel variant K_v7 for seqlen bucket 256, latency improvement 8% vs heuristic. One rollback event recorded (operator-triggered) due to noisy infra; investigating resilience.

2026-03-12 - SRE - Elena Gomez: Added alert for rollback_count. Also suggested rate-limiting probes further when cluster GPU utilization > 85% to avoid noisy results. Action: update probe scheduler to respect utilization threshold.
